title: Writing: A Personal Narrative — A Moment That Changed Something

writingModel.placeholder: Start in medias res — drop the reader into a moment of action or change
writingModel.hint: Use past continuous (scene) + past simple (action) in the opening

writingModel.placeholder: Set the scene — where, when, atmosphere
writingModel.hint: Use past continuous for ongoing background details

writingModel.placeholder: Brief backstory — what had led to this moment
writingModel.hint: Use past perfect for one or two earlier events

writingModel.placeholder: The central event — what happened, in sequence
writingModel.hint: Past simple for the sequence of main actions

writingModel.placeholder: Brief reflection on what the moment meant
writingModel.hint: Return to simple past; avoid slipping into present tense

writingModel.placeholder: A closing image or sentence that resonates
writingModel.hint: Echo the opening if possible; leave the reader with something

writingTemplate.placeholder: Opening sentence — in medias res (e.g. "The train was already moving when she realised...")
writingTemplate.hint: Past continuous + past simple OR strong past simple image

writingTemplate.placeholder: a setting detail (e.g. cold and damp, thick with the smell of rain)
writingTemplate.hint: Use the senses — past simple or past continuous

writingTemplate.suffix: , but she had never expected this.
writingTemplate.hint: Past perfect for one earlier fact; then contrast

writingTemplate.placeholder: the central action or change (e.g. the door swung open)

writingTemplate.hint: Show the reaction through action, not emotion words

writingTemplate.prefix: Later, she would think about that moment —
writingTemplate.placeholder: reflection (e.g. how small it had seemed at the time)
writingTemplate.hint: "Would + think" = looking back from a later point

writingTemplate.placeholder: Final image — echo the opening or leave something unresolved

items: The door was already open when she arrived.
She was halfway there when she remembered.
By the time he reached the platform, the train had gone.
It had been raining for hours when she finally made the call.
Nothing had prepared him for what he saw next.
The streets were empty and slick with rain.
A low hum of conversation filled the room.
The air smelled of coffee and old paper.
Outside, the city was beginning to wake up.
The light was fading, and long shadows stretched across the floor.
She had known this moment would come eventually.
He had spent years preparing for exactly this.
Nothing had changed since she had last been here.
They had met only once before, briefly, at a conference.
She had never quite forgiven herself for what she had said.
Without warning, everything changed.
Suddenly, she understood.
He stopped. He looked up. He said nothing.
She took a breath, and then she did what she had to do.
For a second, neither of them moved.

questions.text: Which is the best opening in medias res?
opts: I am going to tell you about something that happened.
Once upon a time, there was a woman.
The train was already pulling out when she ran onto the platform.
This story is about an important moment in my life.
questions.correct: The train was already pulling out when she ran onto the platform.
questions.hint: In medias res: drop into action without preamble

questions.text: "She ___ (wait) for over an hour before anyone finally noticed her."
questions.hint: Past perfect continuous = ongoing action before narrative present

questions.text: "Without warning, ___." Which correctly completes this for a sudden event?
questions.hint: Past simple for the sudden main action

questions.text: "___, across the hall, someone else was making the same decision." (= at the same time)
questions.hint: "Meanwhile" for simultaneous actions in different locations

questions.text: Which is "showing" not "telling" in narrative writing?
opts: Her voice shook as she tried to speak.
questions.correct: Her voice shook as she tried to speak.
questions.hint: Show emotion through physical detail, not emotion words

questions.text: A strong narrative closing should "resonate" — give the reader something to take away.
"Never ___ he looked back." Choose the correct dramatic inversion form.
"___, she placed the letter on the table and left." (Manner adverb fronted — quietly)
questions.hint: Fronting manner adverb for narrative emphasis
